ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 4 — Focused Visit (Follow-up) — Jack London — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

code.originalText: Six-week review: drinking and PEth, blood pressure, potassium and creatinine, urine albumin, liver tests, mood and safety

text.paragraph: Mr. London has not had a drink since the evening two weeks ago when he sprained his ankle and drank two large whiskies for the pain; he talked that evening through with his counselor and has set a plan for pain and late afternoons. He takes naltrexone every morning without nausea. The ankle is much better with the brace and he has stopped the gel. He writes every morning and swims at the hour he used to take his first drink. He takes losartan 50 mg without dizziness; his home readings average 136/86. He is sleeping six hours. He has had no opioid or anti-inflammatory medicine. His hepatitis B, hepatitis C and HIV tests were negative. [S]
